content.p: The task force on scenarios and models, whose members were selected following the tenth session of the Plenary of the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES) and will serve until the end of the thirteenth session of the Plenary, will oversee and take part in the implementation of the present workplan for objective 4 (b), supported by the technical support unit for scenarios and models at the Institute for Global Environmental Strategies, Japan.
The task force will conduct activities to ensure the effective implementation of the workplan, including the continued monitoring of a set of relevant indicators (see annex VII).

p.i: Deliverable: provision of support on scenarios and models for IPBES assessments

content.p: Activities to provide support on scenarios and models for IPBES assessments will include the provision of advice and input on scenarios and models, including the practical use of scenarios and models and their policy relevance in IPBES assessments in line with the scoping reports. Activities will include the mobilization of experts on scenarios and models and other types of future studies to participate in upcoming assessments, the review of assessment drafts, the engagement of task force members as contributing authors and the provision of webinars and materials, upon request.

p.i: Deliverable: catalysing of the further development of scenarios and models for future IPBES assessments

intro.p: Activities to promote dialogue between IPBES and the community of practice on scenarios and models, including both nature-centred and Mother Earth-centred scenarios and models, and to catalyse the further development of scenarios and models for future IPBES assessments will include:

content.p: Mobilizing existing communities working on scenarios and models and other types of future studies to facilitate the development of scenarios and models relevant to the work of IPBES, thereby also supporting the work of biodiversity-related multilateral environmental agreements;

Continuing the preparation of a compilation of gaps and needs regarding nature-centred scenarios and models set out in completed IPBES assessments and using it to communicate to the scientific community the related needs of IPBES, including through the dedicated space on the IPBES website;

Collecting examples for the development of scenarios using the Nature Futures Framework at various scales and locations and in different contexts, identifying remaining gaps and compiling related information, including comments and critiques contributing to the further development and refinement of methodologies;

Engaging with the communities of experts working on climate and other scenarios and models, including by facilitating the exchange of ideas regarding the further development and use of scenarios and models in IPBES that are also of relevance across multiple intergovernmental processes;

Engaging with various stakeholders, including those with backgrounds in modelling, social sciences, humanities or Indigenous and local knowledge, as well as with policymakers and the private sector, through participation in relevant international meetings and conferences to disseminate, discuss and further develop the work of IPBES on scenarios and models, including the Nature Futures Framework.

attachment.heading: Annex VII to decision IPBES-12/1
attachment.subheading: Indicators for measuring the effectiveness of the implementation of the workplans for objectives 2, 3 and 4 of the rolling work programme up to 2030

FRBRalias.value: Annex VII to decision IPBES-12/1 Indicators for measuring the effectiveness of the implementation of the workplans for objectives 2, 3 and 4 of the rolling work programme up to 2030
FRBRalias.name: title

division.heading: Has IPBES enhanced the capacities of individuals and institutions to strengthen the science-policy interface for biodiversity and ecosystem services?

subdivision.heading: Building capacities to achieve enhanced learning and engagement

content.p: Number of fellows and former fellows selected for intergovernmental science-policy panel roles;
Number of individuals and number of institutions that participated in or used training and familiarization activities and materials (e.g., workshops, webinars, guides and learning tools);
Number of government representatives and number of stakeholders who participated in science-policy dialogue meetings;
Feedback from participants on the usefulness of the capacity-building activity in which they participated.

subdivision.heading: Facilitating access to expertise and information

content.p: Number of capacity-building activities supporting the uptake of IPBES assessments and deliverables that IPBES has been made aware of;
Number of participants and number of institutions taking part in the IPBES capacity-building forum.

subdivision.heading: Strengthening national and regional capacities

content.p: Number of new national and (sub)regional science-policy platforms, networks and assessments that IPBES has been made aware of;
Number of stakeholders and government representatives who participated in online dialogue workshops encouraging the development of national and (sub)regional platforms, networks and assessments.

division.heading: Has IPBES identified, prioritized and facilitated access to existing data and knowledge for use by assessment authors and documented access to data and knowledge contained in completed assessments in an open and reusable way?

intro.p: The reports on the conformity of the assessments with the data and knowledge management policy, prepared by the task force on data and knowledge management for each assessment, remain the main reference for ensuring the effective implementation of the workplans for the data and knowledge management aspect of objective 3 (a) with regard to the work of assessments, and are complemented by additional qualitative indicators focusing on:

content.p: The existence, completeness and clarity of data management reports documenting analytical processes, the tools used and source data;

The structure and maintenance of Zotero libraries, ensuring that each reference is traceable to the chapter in which it was cited, indicated with corresponding tags, and that unused references are removed from final outputs;
The timely uploading of accurate and well-annotated materials, such as chapters, figures, supplementary data and metadata, to Zenodo, with appropriate licensing and metadata citation.
A broader set of indicators to monitor the implementation of the workplan and its contribution to the Platform’s objectives includes:
The existence and recency of updates to the IPBES data and knowledge management policy, long-term vision and associated codes of practice and technical guidelines;
The status and versioning of the IPBES ontology and the number of assessments digitized in accordance with the ontology;
The status and number of records in the assessment library of underlying references;
The number of data sets, data management reports and other knowledge products deposited in long-term open-access repositories, including the number of views and downloads of those products;
The number of entries in the IPBES semantic knowledge base and the volume of activity in associated web services.

division.heading: Has IPBES identified gaps in knowledge and data in its assessments, systematically catalogued them and catalysed the generation of new knowledge by making those gaps known, including to research funding agencies, research programme developers and institutions involved in prioritizing and funding data mobilization?

subdivision.heading: Efforts made to support the identification of knowledge gaps in IPBES assessments and their systematic cataloguing

content.p: Number of knowledge gaps identified in IPBES assessments completed in the intersessional period;
Number of knowledge and data gaps identified in completed IPBES assessments and systematically listed in the online database of identified knowledge gaps.

subdivision.heading: Efforts made to catalyse the generation of new knowledge

content.p: Number of meetings in which the identified gaps were communicated to stakeholders, including research funding agencies, research programme developers and institutions involved in prioritizing and funding data mobilization; number of participants in those meetings and their type and geographical coverage; and the list of IPBES assessments presented at each meeting;
Number of projects and/or amount of funds catalysed to address the knowledge gaps that have been identified in completed IPBES assessments and have been brought to the attention of IPBES.

division.heading: Has IPBES implemented the approach to recognizing and working with Indigenous and local knowledge, including the participatory mechanism established under the approach?

intro.p:
These indicators will be monitored alongside the review of Indigenous and local knowledge in IPBES, which will periodically collect qualitative information from authors and Indigenous Peoples and local communities engaged in IPBES activities. The results of the 2023 review
Available at https://files.ipbes.net/ipbes-web-prod-public-files/2023-06/Review%20of%20Indigenous%20and%20local%20knowledge%20in%20IPBES.pdf. and the 2024 extension of the review
https://files.ipbes.net/ipbes-web-prod-public-files/2024-09/Extension_Review_ILK_IPBES.pdf. are available on the IPBES website.

subdivision.heading: Consideration of Indigenous and local knowledge in assessments

content.p: Numbers of assessment experts in the Indigenous and local knowledge liaison groups of each assessment;
Inclusion of information on Indigenous and local knowledge and/or Indigenous Peoples and local communities in summaries for policymakers;
Number of citations of reports of Indigenous and local knowledge dialogue workshops in assessments;
Whether the task force and the technical support unit provided comments related to Indigenous and local knowledge during external reviews;
Number of items added to the Zotero library on Indigenous and local knowledge.
Participation of Indigenous Peoples and local communities in IPBES processes: number of participants in dialogue workshops, webinars, calls for contributions and other activities.

division.heading: Has IPBES supported the assessment of policy instruments, policy support tools and methodologies in its assessments and enabled the uptake of the findings of the assessments in decision-making?

subdivision.heading: Provision of support to assessments

content.p: Proportion of surveyed policymakers and focal points reporting that IPBES products provide actionable and context-relevant policy options or tools for decision-making;

Number and frequency of explicit references to policy processes and mechanisms in assessment chapters, enabling a clear link to be made between assessment content and the policy context in which the assessment findings might be used.

subdivision.heading: Provision of support for the use of assessments in decision-making

content.p: Number of new or revised international, regional or national policies, strategies or official decisions explicitly referencing or applying findings or policy options from IPBES assessments and other products. To be verified through a review of official policy documents, national biodiversity strategies and action plans and decisions under multilateral environmental agreements and other relevant organizations, data from the IPBES impact-tracking system and reporting from IPBES national focal points.

division.heading: Has IPBES provided advice to assessment authors on the use of existing scenarios and models and catalysed the development of new scenarios and models for the future work of IPBES?

subdivision.heading: Provision of relevant input to IPBES assessments and other IPBES products

content.p: Whether task force members reviewed or contributed to an assessment report or a scoping report;
Degree of satisfaction of assessment experts with webinars and similar events organized for them by the task force (assessed through feedback from participants).

subdivision.heading: Uptake by communities of practice

content.p: Number of scientific papers (peer-reviewed journal articles, book chapters, conference proceedings) and reports published during the intersessional period mentioning the Nature Futures Framework or other scenario and modelling exercises relevant to the work of the task force;
Number of scientific papers (peer-reviewed journal articles, book chapters, conference proceedings) and reports related to the Nature Futures Framework cited during the intersessional period.

subdivision.heading: Outreach and dissemination by the task force

content.p: Degree of satisfaction with workshops, webinars and meetings co-hosted or organized by IPBES to disseminate knowledge to the community of practice (assessed through feedback from participants).

attachment.heading: Decision IPBES-12/2: Organization of the Plenary and dates and venues of future sessions of the Plenary

FRBRalias.value: Decision IPBES-12/2: Organization of the Plenary and dates and venues of future sessions of the Plenary
FRBRalias.name: title

content.p: Decides that the thirteenth session of the Plenary of the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services will be held in the second half of 2027, taking into account the calendar of relevant international meetings;
Invites members of the Platform in a position to do so to consider hosting the thirteenth session of the Plenary;

Requests the Bureau, in close consultation with the members of the Platform, to decide on the specific dates and the venue of the thirteenth session of the Plenary within six months following the twelfth session of the Plenary, taking into account any offers from members to host the session, which should be subject to the successful conclusion of a host country agreement;

Requests the Executive Secretary to conclude and sign a host country agreement for the thirteenth session of the Plenary with the Government of the host State as soon as possible, in conformity with General Assembly resolution 40/243 of 18 December 1985 and in compliance with the provisions of the United Nations administrative instruction on guidelines for the preparation of host Government agreements falling under General Assembly resolution 40/243;
ST/AI/342.

Decides that the fourteenth session of the Plenary of the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services will be held in the second half of 2028, taking into account the calendar of relevant international meetings, in particular under the Convention on Biological Diversity;
Invites members of the Platform in a position to do so to consider hosting the fourteenth session of the Plenary;

Requests the Bureau, in consultation with the members of the Platform, to decide on the specific dates of the fourteenth session of the Plenary, taking into account the calendar of relevant intergovernmental meetings;

Also requests the Bureau, in consultation with members of the Platform, to decide on the venue for the fourteenth session of the Plenary, taking into account any offers from members to host the session, which should be subject to the successful conclusion of a host country agreement;

Requests the Executive Secretary, in the event that the Bureau decides to accept the offer of a specific Government to host the fourteenth session of the Plenary, to conclude and sign a host country agreement with that Government for the fourteenth session of the Plenary as soon as possible, in conformity with General Assembly resolution 40/243 and in compliance with the provisions of the United Nations administrative instruction on guidelines for the preparation of host Government agreements falling under General Assembly resolution 40/243;

Emphasizes that all representatives of members performing functions in connection with the thirteenth and fourteenth sessions of the Plenary should have the right of unimpeded entry into and exit from the host country, and that visas and entry permits, when required, should be granted as speedily as possible and without discrimination;

Invites the Bureau to take the timelines of Platform assessments into account when considering the dates of future sessions of the Plenary, with a view to enabling their timely consideration by relevant bodies under multilateral environmental agreements and policy processes;
Takes note of the draft provisional agendas for the thirteenth and fourteenth sessions of the Plenary, set out in annexes I and II to the present decision;

Requests the Executive Secretary to invite members and observers that are allowed enhanced participation in accordance with decision IPBES-5/4 to provide written comments on the proposed organization of work of the thirteenth session of the Plenary;

Also requests the Executive Secretary to finalize the proposed organization of work for the thirteenth session of the Plenary in line with comments received at the twelfth session of the Plenary and written comments received in response to the invitation referred to in paragraph 13 above.

Taking note also of the pledges made for the period beyond 2025,

Noting the urgent need to reduce transaction costs and to significantly increase the funds raised to implement the rolling work programme up to 2030 and to ensure the sustainability of the trust fund of the Platform,
Noting with concern the limited number of members contributing to the trust fund, and the limited progress made in increasing that number,

Noting the need to enhance efforts to broaden the donor base to encourage non-contributing members of the Platform and public organizations to support the work of the Platform, and the limited progress made in that regard,
Taking note of the status of expenditures in 2024, as listed in table 4, set out in the annex to the present decision,
Taking note also of the savings of $3.2 million in the final expenditures in 2024 compared with the approved budget,
Noting ongoing efforts to achieve savings and the need to increase the efficiency of managing expenditures without compromising the quality of deliverables of the Platform,

Noting also that the costs indicated in the provisional budget for 2028 will be adjusted to reflect the activities required to implement the objectives of the Platform, thereby duly accounting for the overall cost developments for further consideration at the thirteenth session of the Plenary,
Recalling the financial procedures for the Platform adopted in decision IPBES-2/7 and amended in decision IPBES-3/2, in particular rules 4, 5 and 10,

content.p:
Welcomes the fundraising efforts undertaken by the Executive Secretary in response to decision IPBES-11/3;
As reported in document IPBES/12/5.
Urges the Executive Secretary to explore all available options within budgetary limits to reinforce the fundraising unit of the secretariat;

Urges Governments, including regional economic integration organizations, in a position to do so to support the work of the Platform by making pledges and contributions to the trust fund of the Platform, as well as in-kind contributions;

Requests the Executive Secretary and the Bureau to explore additional opportunities and make further efforts to actively communicate the importance of the work of the Platform and its benefits to potential donors, in particular to non-contributing members of the Platform, through the United Nations system-wide network and locations and other means;

Requests the Executive Secretary, taking into account the respective fair share of voluntary contributions and, where relevant, indicating that information in letters, to encourage members to support the work of the Platform;
Invites the four United Nations collaborative partners of the Platform to increase support for the fundraising efforts of the Executive Secretary;

Invites United Nations bodies, the Global Environment Facility, other intergovernmental organizations, the private sector, foundations, stakeholders and others in a position to do so to support the work of the Platform, in particular through contributions to the trust fund;

Requests the Executive Secretary to report on expenditures for 2025 and 2026, and to explore ways to reduce transaction costs and administrative burdens associated with the in-kind and cash contributions and to report accordingly to the Plenary at its thirteenth session;

Requests the Bureau and the Executive Secretary to take into consideration the recommendations of the report on the midterm review regarding financial and budgetary arrangements when implementing the present decision;

Requests the Executive Secretary, the Bureau and the Multidisciplinary Expert Panel to ensure that the proposal on Platform deliverables referred to in paragraph 6 of decision IPBES-12/1 is consistent with the projected financial resources of the Platform;

Urges nominating Governments and those in a position to do so to provide funding to Indigenous Peoples and local communities and youth representatives to increase their participation in the full range of activities of the Platform;
Adopts the revised budget for 2026, amounting to $8,506,369, as set out in table 5 of the annex to the present decision;
Also adopts the revised budget for 2027, amounting to $9,569,126, as set out in table 6 of the annex to the present decision;
Further adopts the provisional budget for 2028, amounting to $9,490,117, as set out in table 7 of the annex to the present decision.
